A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeGauss research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and novel-view synthesis results, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2, ablations in Table 3, and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds efficiency measurements, RobustNeRF results, and qualitative DyCheck-iPhone and Bonn RGBD evaluations.

M1.justification: The Gaussian branches, composition and brightness masks, losses, opacity resets and optional pruning remain unchanged. Section 3.6 explains the existing procedure differently; the added densification-threshold comparison is an experimental configuration change.

E1.justification: Appendices F–H add strict-monocular novel-view synthesis on DyCheck-iPhone, RGB-only reconstruction of Bonn RGBD's Crowd scene, and the Android, Crab2, Statue and Yoda scenes from RobustNeRF. These substantially broaden evaluation coverage while retaining the original datasets.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain intact. New Figure 14 adds HyperNeRF, Dynamic 3D Gaussians and Deformable 3D Gaussians alongside 4DGS in a qualitative monocular comparison. Table 4 also extends efficiency comparisons to previously evaluated Neu3D baselines.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds configurations with doubled densification gradient thresholds for both DeGauss and 4DGS, comparing quality, speed, training time and Gaussian counts. The original splits, image-quality metrics and training iteration budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a controlled densification-threshold comparison examining the relationship between Gaussian count, rendering speed and reconstruction quality. The original brightness-control, opacity-reset, background-mask and depth-loss ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 1 retains the same ±0.005 qualification for rounding uncertainty in DeSplat scores.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add efficiency and RobustNeRF results, while Figures 14–16 add qualitative findings. Table 2 changes DeGauss's CutBeef PSNR from 32.54 to 32.56. Figures 1 and 7 change its FPS labels from 64 to 151 and 71 to 157. Table 4 retains 71 FPS for the default configuration and reports 157 for the doubled-threshold variant, so these annotations do not establish same-setting version-to-version gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 3 and Appendices A–B, including losses and pruning criteria, are retained. The revised rendering discussion adds qualitative explanation rather than a new derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about self-supervised decomposition, distractor-free reconstruction and efficient dynamic modeling. The appendix additions provide further support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.6 adds a more specific explanation involving early ray termination in coupled NeRF rendering and gradient flow through independently rasterized branches. New appendix discussion connects the representation to monocular generalization and editing applications. Existing limitations concerning static ambiguities, camera poses and utility-Gaussian overhead are retained.

D1.justification: The Bonn experiment specifies 928 RGB frames and SfM/MVS preprocessing. Table 4 newly reports training times and dynamic-Gaussian counts, including 2.1 hours for default DeGauss and 2 hours for its modified configuration. Existing implementation details and access information remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gao et al.'s Monocular Dynamic View Synthesis: A Reality Check and Palazzolo et al.'s ReFusion for the additional datasets. It also expands the comparison with coupled NeRF rendering, while the dedicated related-work section remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: Section 3.6 is rewritten, four appendix subsections are inserted, existing visualization and discussion sections are renumbered, and acknowledgments and small header edits are added. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: New Tables 4–5 and Figures 14–16 substantially expand the displayed evidence with efficiency comparisons and three additional evaluation settings. Figure 1's imagery and caption are revised, and Table 3 moves from page 9 to page 8. Most existing experimental figures retain their images.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–5 and Figures 14–16 strengthen support for generalization and expose useful quality, speed and training-cost tradeoffs; Section 3.6 also explains the design more clearly. The gain is limited by qualitative-only monocular and crowd examples and brief documentation of the added protocols. The higher reported FPS involves a changed configuration rather than an established same-setting advance.
